_comment: Réécritures de phrases dont un chiffre est faux ou non sourçable. Le JUGEMENT vit ici, relisible ; l'APPLICATION est faite par tools/build-substack-episode.js, qui échoue si un texte source est introuvable — sans quoi une correction obsolète deviendrait un silence.
_principe: Deux motifs seulement. (1) CHIFFRE FAUX, vérifié aux barres : les faits datés de la série gap-risk annonçaient tous « opened X% lower » en donnant la variation de CLÔTURE. Dans une série qui enseigne que c'est l'écart d'OUVERTURE qui coûte, c'est la leçon elle-même qui était fausse. (2) AGRÉGAT NON SOURÇABLE : une statistique de population que les sources citées ne publient pas. On garde la direction, on retire la fausse précision — un chiffre inventé n'instruit pas, il fabrique de la confiance.

gap-risk-survival/episode-01.md.from: This is not rare. Across the S&P 500 from 2000 to 2024, about 68% of sessions opened away from the previous session's close. Median gap, 0.4% — noise. But roughly 12 gaps a year exceed 1%, and two or three exceed 2%. Mondays run largest, averaging 0.52% against 0.35% on Wednesdays, because the weekend hands the open two extra days of news. Downside gaps are also bigger than upside ones: −2.1% average against +1.4%, a ratio near 1.5. Margin calls force selling, clustered stops cascade, and market makers widen spreads precisely when you need depth.
gap-risk-survival/episode-01.md.to: This is not rare, and it is not symmetric. Most sessions open a little away from the previous close, and almost all of that is noise. A handful each year are not. Mondays tend to open furthest from Friday, because the weekend hands the open two extra days of news with no market to absorb it. And downside gaps run larger than upside ones, for a mechanical reason: margin calls force selling, clustered stops cascade into each other, and market makers widen spreads precisely when you need depth. We are not going to hand you a distribution here — measure it yourself, on your own instruments and your own reference price, because a number quoted without its sample is worth nothing.

gap-risk-survival/episode-01.md.from: Single stocks make the index numbers look gentle. On 3 February 2022 Meta opened 26.4% lower after its first decline in daily users, erasing about $230 billion of market value overnight. A 10% stop delivered a 26% loss.
gap-risk-survival/episode-01.md.to: Single stocks make index averages look gentle. On 3 February 2022, after reporting its first decline in daily users, Meta closed at 323.00 the day before and opened at 244.65 — **24.3% lower, before a single share changed hands in the regular session**. It ended that day 26.4% below the prior close. Both numbers matter, and they are not the same number: a stop set 10% below the close was passed over at the opening print, not filled on the way down.

gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.from: Start with plain funds. Average absolute overnight moves sit near 0.35% for the S&P 500 tracker, 0.48% for the Nasdaq-100, 0.55% for small caps, 0.25% for gold. A fund holding 500 companies dilutes any single blow-up. But in a systemic shock everything moves together and dilution stops helping: on 16 March 2020 those same funds opened −8.1%, −9.3% and −10.2%.
gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.to: Start with plain funds. On an ordinary night a broad tracker moves a fraction of a percent, a narrower index a little more, small caps more again — measure it on the funds you actually hold rather than trusting a figure someone quoted. A fund holding 500 companies dilutes any single blow-up. But in a systemic shock everything moves together and dilution stops helping: in March 2020 the broad trackers all gapped down together, by high single digits, on the same mornings.

gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.from: Single companies concentrate the danger and publish the schedule. Earnings land four times a year, after the close or before the open. Typical moves run ±5–8% for large caps, ±10–20% for mid and small caps, ±20–50% for growth and biotech. Netflix opened 35.1% lower on 20 April 2022 after losing subscribers for the first time in a decade, about $54 billion gone. Nvidia opened 24.4% higher on 25 May 2023 on guidance of roughly $11 billion against the $7 billion expected. And the calendar does not cover everything: Apple opened 9.9% lower on 2 January 2019 after a guidance letter nobody had on their diary.
gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.to: Single companies concentrate the danger and publish the schedule. Earnings land four times a year, after the close or before the open, and the size of the reaction scales with how much of the story is still unproven. Two measured examples, opening print against the previous close: Netflix closed at 34.86 on 19 April 2022 and opened at 24.52 the next morning after losing subscribers for the first time in a decade — **29.7% lower at the open**, and 35.1% lower by the close. Nvidia went the other way on 25 May 2023: 30.54 the night before, **38.52 at the open, up 26.1%**, closing +24.4%. Note that the opening gap and the day's change disagree in both cases, and in opposite directions. And the calendar does not cover everything — a guidance letter can arrive on a date nobody had in their diary.

gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.from: Digital assets trade around the clock, but continuous timestamps do not mean continuous liquidity: CME bitcoin futures close Friday evening and reopen Sunday, and roughly 85% of weekends leave a gap averaging about 2.3%.
gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.to: Digital assets trade around the clock, but continuous timestamps do not mean continuous liquidity: CME bitcoin futures close Friday evening and reopen Sunday, and the spot market keeps moving in between. The weekend gap on the futures contract is a recurring feature, not an occasional accident — check the contract specification for the exact halt, and measure the gap distribution yourself before you size around it.

gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.why: « more than 100,000 retail accounts went negative » : aucune source ne publie de décompte de comptes. Ce qui est documenté, ce sont des montants — 225 M$ de soldes débiteurs chez FXCM, ~120 M$ chez Interactive Brokers, plus d'un milliard d'appels de marge sur l'industrie. Remplacer un décompte invérifiable par les montants qui le sont ne coûte rien à la démonstration et lui donne une source.

gap-risk-survival/episode-02.md.to: One broker failed, another was left with $225 million of client debit balances, and industry-wide margin calls ran past $1 billion.

gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.why: Les deux exemples chiffrés de l'épisode étaient présentés comme des trades RÉALISÉS, avec leur résultat. Vérification aux barres MCP : aucun des deux ne s'est produit ainsi. Nvidia le 25/05/2023, en base ajustée du fractionnement 10:1 (cohérente avec l'épisode 02) — clôture de la veille 30,54, ouverture 38,52, soit +26,1 % et non « 306 → 380, environ 24 % ». Surtout, le PLUS HAUT de séance fut 39,48 : un objectif à 39,5 (395 non ajusté) n'a jamais imprimé, et la phrase « $395 printed inside 40 minutes » est fausse. Réécrit pour enseigner la géométrie du plan, qui est la leçon, sans affirmer un résultat qui n'a pas eu lieu.
gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.verified: QueryData bars_daily NVDA 2023-05-23→26 : 24/05 close 30.538 ; 25/05 open 38.5229, high 39.4799, low 36.6349, close 37.9799.
gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.from: **Continuation.** Price holds away from the old range and builds a new one. Nvidia raised its guidance in May 2023. The stock closed at $306 and opened the next session at $380, up about 24%. The continuation plan waited for the first five-minute bar to close green, bought at $382, and put invalidation at $374 — the low of that bar, not a round number and not the loss the trader would have preferred. The objective sat at $395, on VWAP (the day's average traded price, weighted by volume) plus an extension. $395 printed inside 40 minutes: 2.1% risked, 3.4% made, about 1.6 back per unit of risk.
gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.to: **Continuation.** Price holds away from the old range and builds a new one. Nvidia raised its guidance in May 2023: the stock closed at 30.54 and opened the next session at 38.52, up 26.1% — prices on the basis adjusted for the later ten-for-one split, so they match a chart you would pull up today. A continuation plan names its trigger before the open. Wait for the first five-minute bar to close green, buy just above it, put invalidation at that bar's low. The low comes from structure, not from the loss the trader would have preferred. The objective sits on VWAP — the day's average traded price, weighted by volume — plus an extension. Where you set that objective is what decides whether the plan pays: the session high was 39.48, so anything set above it went unfilled no matter how sound the reasoning behind it.

gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.why: L'exemple bitcoin était inventé de bout en bout. Aucun vendredi de janvier 2024 ne clôture à 43 200, et le week-end suivant la clôture du 12 janvier (42 853) voit le comptant BAISSER — plus hauts 43 235 le 13 et 43 066 le 14 — jamais 45 800. Le trade « vendu vers 45 800, objectif 43 200, revenu en trois jours, 2,6 % risqués et 5,7 % gagnés » n'a pas eu lieu. Le PHÉNOMÈNE, lui, est réel et suffit à la leçon : les futures CME s'arrêtent le vendredi soir et rouvrent le dimanche pendant que le comptant continue.
gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.from: **Rejection.** Price cannot hold the gap and falls back into the old range. CME bitcoin futures close Friday at 5 p.m. New York and reopen Sunday at 6 p.m., while spot bitcoin trades straight through. In January 2024 the futures closed Friday at $43,200, spot ran to $45,800 over the weekend on spot-ETF news, and the futures reopened roughly 6% higher. The rejection plan sold near $45,800, aimed at that Friday close of $43,200, and set invalidation at $47,000, one and a half times the size of the gap. Price came back in three days: 2.6% risked, 5.7% made, about 2.2 per unit.
gap-risk-survival/episode-04.md.to: **Rejection.** Price cannot hold the gap and falls back into the old range. The structural case is bitcoin: CME futures close Friday at 5 p.m. New York and reopen Sunday at 6 p.m., while spot trades straight through. Whatever the spot market does in those forty-nine hours arrives at the futures open in a single print. A rejection plan therefore names the level it expects price to fail at, takes its objective from the last price the halted market agreed on — that Friday close — and puts invalidation beyond the gap rather than inside it, because a gap that is going to fill rarely fills in a straight line. What it must never assume is that the gap fills at all. Around the spot-ETF approvals in January 2024, bitcoin closed one Friday at 42,853 and then spent the weekend going nowhere: the two weekend sessions topped out at 43,235 and 43,066, and the following Monday closed lower still, at 42,512. There was no gap to fade. A plan that only works when the gap is large is not a plan.

La leçon — détenir du haut rendement comme lest, c'est détenir du risque actions — ne bouge pas d'un pouce. La corrélation 0,70, elle, est vérifiée à 0,68.

market-checklist/episode-01.md.why: PASSAGE FABRIQUÉ, le plus grave du corpus. Aucun CPI n'est sorti le 13 mars 2026 — c'était un vendredi ; celui de février est paru le mercredi 11 mars à 8h30 New York, à +2,4 % et non +3,1 %. Le VIX n'a jamais imprimé 29,4 ce jour-là : son plus haut fut 28,47, sa clôture 27,19. Et 14h30 UTC ne correspond à aucun horaire de publication BLS. Réécrit sur la vraie séance — et le passage en sort PLUS COHÉRENT avec la thèse de l'épisode : la publication n'a pas fait le choc (le VIX a clôturé plus bas le 11), c'est la dérive des deux séances suivantes qui a fait le régime.
market-checklist/episode-01.md.verified: CPI février 2026 publié le 11/03/2026 à 8h30 ET, +2,4 % sur douze mois (cœur +2,5 %). ^VIX : 11/03 plus haut 26,23, clôture 24,23 ; 13/03 ouverture 27,85, plus haut 28,47, plus bas 24,67, clôture 27,19. TLT 13/03 : −0,50 %. UUP : +0,76 %.
market-checklist/episode-01.md.from: Here is what that looked like on 13 March 2026. Inflation came in at +3.1% at 14:30 UTC. Within the hour the VIX printed 29.4, long Treasuries were sold hard, the dollar bounced, and the score landed at 31 out of 100. The playbook that day was straightforward: no growth exposure, hedges on, cash for the rest, and no new unhedged longs until the VIX settled back under 25.
market-checklist/episode-01.md.to: Here is what that looked like in the second week of March 2026. Inflation came in at +2.4% at 8:30 New York time on the eleventh — cooler than feared, and the VIX closed that day at 24.2, below where it opened. No shock. Two sessions later, with nothing new published, it closed at 27.2, long Treasuries were drifting lower and the dollar had firmed. The release was not the event. The drift around it was, and the score fell into the low thirties on the back of it. The playbook at that level is straightforward: no growth exposure, hedges on, cash for the rest, and no new unhedged longs until the VIX settles back under 25.

market-checklist/episode-01.md.why: Deux des trois relevés VIX de la trajectoire étaient faux de deux à cinq points : 24,1 fin février contre 19,9 réels, 22,8 le 10 mars contre 24,9. Avec les vraies valeurs, le VIX MONTE tout du long, alors que le score du texte montait de 46 à 52 — la trajectoire du score devenait incohérente avec ses propres intrants. Le score étant un composite maison que je ne peux pas reconstruire a posteriori, je retire les valeurs datées que rien ne soutient et garde la seule chose mesurable : la montée continue de la volatilité. Les bandes de score restent au paragraphe suivant, où elles relèvent de la politique de risque et non de la mesure.
market-checklist/episode-01.md.from: The score had been sliding for weeks before that. Late January it read 68. End of February, 46, with the VIX at 24.1 and liquidity contracting. On 10 March it was 52, VIX 22.8, index caught between its two averages. Nothing dramatic happened on any single day.
market-checklist/episode-01.md.to: The pressure had been building for weeks before that. At the end of February the VIX sat at 19.9 and liquidity was contracting. By 10 March it had reached 24.9, with the index caught between its two averages. Nothing dramatic happened on any single day.

trade-signal-check/episode-06.md.why: Le « while » opposait deux valeurs IDENTIQUES : « the archived decision bar closed at $12.095, while the raw screen used $12.095 ». Le fond est juste — l'archive et l'écran disent 12,095, le plan retient 12,25, et c'est cette transformation non tracée que la porte 7 attrape — mais la phrase place le contraste au mauvais endroit et se lit comme une coquille. Reformulée sans introduire aucun chiffre.
trade-signal-check/episode-06.md.verified: Aucune donnée de marché en jeu : c'est la structure de la phrase qui était fautive, pas ses valeurs.
